version.changelog:
- Expanded documentation in SKILL.md with a Docker-based Stirling-PDF deployment guide and initial API key setup instructions.
- Added project introduction and "About Stirling-PDF" section for context and feature overview.
- Included a health check endpoint in the quick reference.
- Clarified environment variable usage and endpoint notes.
- Improved formatting and streamlined quick reference examples.

llm.summary: Review before installing because the skill handles sensitive PDFs through API uploads, and one helper script can send documents and the API key to an undocumented private-network address.

dimensions.detail: The PDF operations are purpose-aligned for a Stirling-PDF wrapper, but the documentation strongly claims local/no-upload processing while scripts submit files to HTTP API endpoints; one script defaults to http://192.168.31.158:3998 rather than localhost or the documented variable.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The docs disclose an API server and API key, but runtime commands do not warn before uploading PDFs, and scripts/stirling-pdf.sh uses eval with user-supplied merge filenames, creating avoidable command-execution risk from crafted file names.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is documentation-only Docker setup using frooodle/s-pdf:latest, persistent /opt volumes, and --restart unless-stopped; this is visible and coherent for self-hosting, but users should understand it creates a persistent local service.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending PDFs, passwords, and security-operation inputs to a configured Stirling-PDF service can be proportionate, but the hard-coded private IP default and inconsistent STIRLING_API_URL versus documented STIRLING_BASE_URL make the actual destination under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden persistence, privilege escalation, or background agent behavior was found in the skill scripts; persistence is limited to the disclosed Docker container restart policy and mounted data/log directories.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you operate or explicitly trust the Stirling-PDF server that will receive the PDFs. Set the server URL explicitly before use, avoid the helper script defaulting to 192.168.31.158, and treat uploaded PDFs, document passwords, and signing material as sensitive. Use decrypt/sign features only for documents you are authorized to modify.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: API-based processing is expected for Stirling-PDF, but the artifact also claims no uploads/data stays private and one helper defaults to an undocumented private-network endpoint, so the concern is materially supported.
[SDI-2] expected: An API key is expected for a secured self-hosted Stirling-PDF instance and is tagged in metadata, but the documentation and helper scripts are inconsistent about the base URL variable and destination.
[SQP-2] expected: Decrypt, encrypt, watermark, and signing endpoints are normal PDF-toolkit capabilities, but the skill provides little caution about authorization, sensitive passwords, or integrity-sensitive signing workflows.
[SQP-2] expected: OCR, merge, compress, conversion, and blank-page removal all upload local files to the configured API service; this is coherent for an API wrapper, but the no-upload wording and lack of runtime disclosure make it a Review concern.
